statement: TSMC's CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity, not silicon wafer starts or HBM memory itself, is the binding constraint on AI accelerator supply through 2026-2027, and because allocation is won through committed multi-year volume rather than spot orders, the constraint is reinforcing the position of the largest, best-capitalized buyers (Nvidia and Broadcom's six anchor custom-ASIC customers) rather than expanding total industry throughput. UPDATE (2026-09-05): this packaging-specific claim is now downgraded -- TrendForce reports the CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026 on a ~10x capacity build-out since 2023, and OpenAI's first Broadcom-designed chip (Jalapeno) shipped in Q3 FY2026 without a packaging-related delay. See the companion thesis thesis-broadcom-ai-backlog-custom-asic-design-bottleneck for the current, more concentration-focused framing.

kill_conditions.condition: CoWoS lead times normalize or capacity is confirmed no longer fully booked
kill_conditions.metric: TSMC management commentary on CoWoS booking status / reported packaging lead times
kill_conditions.threshold: TSMC states CoWoS capacity is no longer fully booked for the year, or reported lead times fall to industry-typical levels

kill_conditions.condition: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue misses guidance
kill_conditions.metric: Quarterly AI semiconductor revenue vs. guided figure
kill_conditions.threshold: Actual revenue below the guided figure by a material margin for two consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Major AI capex slowdown announced by hyperscaler customers
kill_conditions.metric: Aggregate hyperscaler capex guidance (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon)
kill_conditions.threshold: Aggregate guided capex growth decelerates materially quarter over quarter

statement: Nvidia's push to mobilize over $500 billion in third-party financing does not resolve a capital-quantity bottleneck -- global private credit and alternative-asset capacity is abundant and readily deployed -- but it does not resolve the harder constraint either: credible, arm's-length underwriting capacity for AI compute as loan collateral remains scarce because no large AI GPU cluster has yet completed a full multi-year depreciation and resale cycle, leaving lenders, regulators (BIS), and credit markets (Nvidia's own record CDS spread) unable to price the risk with confidence, while Nvidia's simultaneous role as chip vendor, prospective guarantor, and financing orchestrator is what critics label 'circular financing.'

kill_conditions.condition: Definitive financing-platform agreements are disclosed with fully transparent, conventional, arm's-length terms that do not depend on Nvidia guarantees, Nvidia equity stakes in borrowers, or overlapping collateral
kill_conditions.metric: Disclosed terms of the six financing platforms
kill_conditions.threshold: Publicly disclosed agreement terms show no Nvidia guarantee or equity linkage to borrowing counterparties

kill_conditions.condition: Nvidia and hyperscaler credit-risk pricing normalizes despite continued AI capex growth
kill_conditions.metric: Nvidia 5-year CDS spread and hyperscaler investment-grade bond spreads
kill_conditions.threshold: Sustained normalization to roughly pre-2026 levels (around 40 basis points or below for Nvidia CDS) for at least one full quarter

kill_conditions.condition: Realized secondary-market resale prices for 3+ year old AI GPU clusters come in at or above industry bull-case retention estimates
kill_conditions.metric: Observed secondary-market GPU resale values as a percentage of original price
kill_conditions.threshold: Verified resale transactions at or above roughly 50% of original value at three years

statement: As TSMC's CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity closes in on demand after tripling-plus over three years, the AI accelerator supply chain's binding structural constraint is shifting one layer upstream to ABF dielectric film and the IC substrates built from it: Ajinomoto's estimated 95%+ share of global ABF film supply, its Q3 2026 30% price increase, and multi-year, multi-billion-dollar capacity build-outs at substrate makers Ibiden and Unimicron (each targeting 2028 or later for major new capacity) together indicate that packaging is no longer the tightest link -- materials and substrate fabrication now are, and by the strict definition used in this research (extreme demand, low supply elasticity, hard substitutability), this node qualifies as a genuine structural bottleneck where CoWoS assembly increasingly does not.

kill_conditions.condition: Ajinomoto or a credible alternative ABF material supplier brings meaningful new capacity online well ahead of the reported 2032 target, or a qualified substitute dielectric material is adopted in volume by a top-tier substrate maker for AI-grade substrates
kill_conditions.metric: Announced/confirmed new ABF-equivalent material capacity or qualified substitute adoption
kill_conditions.threshold: New capacity equal to at least 10% of current global ABF supply confirmed online, or a qualified substitute material adopted in volume production by at least one top-3 substrate maker

kill_conditions.condition: The ABF substrate supply-demand gap, as tracked by industry analysts, narrows materially or turns to surplus well before the 2027-2028 window currently projected
kill_conditions.metric: Industry-analyst-reported ABF substrate supply-demand gap percentage
kill_conditions.threshold: Gap falls below roughly 10% or flips to surplus within the next 12-18 months

kill_conditions.condition: AI hyperscaler capital-expenditure guidance decelerates materially, reducing downstream demand for AI accelerators and therefore ABF substrates
kill_conditions.metric: Aggregate hyperscaler capital-expenditure growth guidance (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon)
kill_conditions.threshold: Aggregate guided capex growth decelerates materially quarter over quarter

statement: SK Hynix's, Samsung's, and Micron's 2026 results and guidance indicate that High Bandwidth Memory has become the AI accelerator supply chain's most severe and longest-duration structural bottleneck: HBM4 mass production is ramping under long-term agreements, HBM's roughly 3-to-1 wafer-consumption ratio against conventional DRAM is driving a parallel commodity-memory price shock, and SK Hynix's own CEO and controlling shareholder have publicly warned the shortage persists beyond 2030 -- longer than either the CoWoS packaging constraint (now easing) or the ABF-substrate constraint (targeted 2028-2032) this pipeline previously examined. Credible analysts disagree sharply on durability: some argue the shortage already peaked in Q2 2026 and could tip toward oversupply by 2028 as incumbent capacity, plus China's fast-scaling CXMT, lands simultaneously.

kill_conditions.condition: Independent analyst tracking confirms supply-demand stabilizing or surplus well ahead of the 2029-2030 timeline SK Hynix leadership has forecast
kill_conditions.metric: Reported memory supply-demand sufficiency ratio / industry inventory levels
kill_conditions.threshold: Credible industry-analyst data showing the DRAM/HBM market at or near balance by Q4 2027 rather than 2029-2030

kill_conditions.condition: CXMT or another new entrant brings qualified, volume HBM4-class output online at a scale materially exceeding current projections well ahead of 2028
kill_conditions.metric: CXMT (or other new entrant) HBM wafer starts per month, and evidence of qualification by a top-tier AI accelerator customer
kill_conditions.threshold: New entrant HBM output reaching at least 10% of incumbent combined HBM capacity, with at least one qualified design win outside China, within the next 2 years

kill_conditions.condition: AI hyperscaler capital-expenditure guidance decelerates materially, reducing downstream demand for AI accelerators and therefore HBM
kill_conditions.metric: Aggregate hyperscaler capital-expenditure growth guidance (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon)
kill_conditions.threshold: Aggregate guided capex growth decelerates materially quarter over quarter

statement: Record 2026 order backlogs and multi-year lead times at Siemens Energy, GE Vernova, and Hitachi Energy -- the three largest Western suppliers of large power transformers -- combined with reporting that 30-50% of 2026's planned US AI data-center capacity is being delayed or canceled specifically for lack of transformers and switchgear, indicate that grid equipment has emerged as a structural bottleneck on AI infrastructure that is more immediate and broader in scope than the chip-side constraints (CoWoS packaging, ABF substrates, HBM memory) this pipeline has previously examined, because it gates every data center regardless of which AI chip it houses. The root constraint traces further upstream to grain-oriented electrical steel (GOES), which has a single, comparatively lower-grade domestic US source. Billions of dollars in new transformer manufacturing capacity are under construction, but analysts and manufacturers consistently place meaningful relief no earlier than 2027-2028.

kill_conditions.condition: Publicly reported tier-1 OEM lead times for large power transformers shorten materially from the 48-60+ month range currently cited
kill_conditions.metric: Quoted large-power-transformer lead time (months) at Siemens Energy, GE Vernova, and Hitachi Energy
kill_conditions.threshold: Lead times fall below 24 months at two or more of the three major suppliers

kill_conditions.condition: The share of planned US data-center capacity delayed or canceled for electrical-equipment reasons falls well below the 30-50% range reported for 2026
kill_conditions.metric: Reported share of planned annual US data-center capacity (GW) delayed or canceled specifically for power-equipment shortages
kill_conditions.threshold: Reported delay/cancellation rate attributable to electrical equipment falls below 15% for a full calendar year

kill_conditions.condition: AI hyperscaler capital-expenditure guidance decelerates materially, reducing downstream demand for new data-center capacity and therefore grid equipment
kill_conditions.metric: Aggregate hyperscaler capital-expenditure growth guidance (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon)
kill_conditions.threshold: Aggregate guided capex growth decelerates materially quarter over quarter

statement: Copper prices near all-time highs, a fresh DRC export ban on copper and cobalt concentrate, and a tariff-driven US stockpiling squeeze together indicate copper has joined chip packaging, substrates, memory and grid transformers as a physical constraint on the AI buildout, but the evidence for copper specifically as an AI-caused structural bottleneck is weaker and more contested than for those prior nodes: AI data centers are estimated to draw only ~475,000 tonnes of copper in 2026, under 2% of the ~28.7-million-tonne global refined market, and the major forecasters disagree sharply on whether the overall market is even in deficit -- ICSG's own forecast flipped from a 150,000-tonne deficit (October 2025) to a 96,000-tonne surplus (April 2026) for the same calendar year. What is not contested is supply-side rigidity: new mine production takes an average 17.9 years from discovery, with permitting alone now stretching toward 30 years in some jurisdictions -- a genuinely low-elasticity, hard-to-substitute (for mission-critical power distribution) upstream node whose recent price spike looks substantially driven by tariff-anticipation stockpiling and the DRC's new export restriction rather than AI demand alone.

kill_conditions.condition: A major forecaster (ICSG, Wood Mackenzie, or S&P Global) confirms a full-year refined copper surplus for 2026
kill_conditions.metric: Annual global refined copper supply-demand balance
kill_conditions.threshold: A confirmed surplus of at least 50,000 tonnes is reported for calendar year 2026 by two or more of ICSG, Wood Mackenzie, or S&P Global

kill_conditions.condition: Copper prices retreat sharply from current near-record levels
kill_conditions.metric: LME three-month copper price
kill_conditions.threshold: Sustained decline below $10,000/tonne for a full calendar quarter

kill_conditions.condition: AI hyperscaler capital-expenditure guidance decelerates materially, reducing downstream copper demand growth
kill_conditions.metric: Aggregate hyperscaler capital-expenditure growth guidance (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon)
kill_conditions.threshold: Aggregate guided capex growth decelerates materially quarter over quarter

kill_conditions.condition: The DRC's concentrate export ban is reversed, eased, or shown to have negligible effect on refined copper supply
kill_conditions.metric: DRC export policy status and refined-copper flow from DRC-sourced concentrate to global smelters
kill_conditions.threshold: Ban is formally reversed or eased within 6 months, or independent reporting shows no material disruption to smelter concentrate supply

statement: EML laser fabrication for 800G/1.6T optical transceivers is a genuine near-term structural bottleneck on AI GPU-cluster networking -- demand is extreme, only a handful of companies worldwide can fabricate qualifying-yield InP-based lasers, and substitutability is hard for high-speed long-reach interconnects -- evidenced by Nvidia's unprecedented March 2026 direct $4 billion investment in its two largest suppliers (Coherent and Lumentum) to secure capacity. However, InP and transceiver-module capacity can roughly double within 12-18 months, far faster than the mining, grid-equipment, or advanced-packaging bottlenecks this pipeline has previously examined, creating a genuine 2027 oversupply risk if hyperscaler capital-expenditure growth decelerates from its 2026 pace.

kill_conditions.condition: InP/EML lead times normalize to pre-2026 industry-typical levels
kill_conditions.metric: Reported EML laser and 800G/1.6T transceiver lead times
kill_conditions.threshold: Lead times reported at or below 20 weeks for two consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Hyperscaler capital-expenditure guidance decelerates materially, reducing downstream optical-networking demand growth
kill_conditions.metric: Aggregate hyperscaler capital-expenditure growth guidance (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon)
kill_conditions.threshold: Aggregate guided capex growth decelerates materially quarter over quarter, toward the 30-50% range flagged by analysts

kill_conditions.condition: Coherent's or Lumentum's own revenue growth or bookings decelerate sharply despite continued industry capex growth, signaling early inventory correction
kill_conditions.metric: Quarter-over-quarter revenue growth and book-to-bill ratio at Coherent and Lumentum
kill_conditions.threshold: Sequential revenue growth turns negative or book-to-bill falls below 1.0 for two consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Co-packaged optics adoption accelerates faster than expected, reducing discrete pluggable-transceiver demand
kill_conditions.metric: Reported CPO switch/GPU shipment volumes as a share of total AI-cluster networking ports
kill_conditions.threshold: CPO ports exceed 25% of new AI-cluster networking deployments within the next year

statement: Helium is a genuine structural bottleneck behind AI-driven semiconductor fabrication -- a non-substitutable input to wafer crystal growth, cooling and leak detection, concentrated in a war-damaged Qatari complex (QatarEnergy's own estimate: up to five years to repair) with its sole maritime export route (the Strait of Hormuz) collapsed for months. Unlike this pipeline's prior AI-demand-driven bottlenecks, this is a supply-side geopolitical shock that AI/electronics demand happens to be absorbing fastest. Its durability is genuinely contested: TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix hold multi-month buffers and high recycling rates that blunt near-term impact, industrial gas majors (Air Products, Linde) describe helium as margin-neutral-to-dilutive rather than a windfall, and Linde does not expect normalization before early 2027.

kill_conditions.condition: Strait of Hormuz shipping normalizes
kill_conditions.metric: Daily ship transit count (Lloyd's List Intelligence and similar trackers)
kill_conditions.threshold: Transits recover to at least 70 ships/day (roughly 80% of the ~85/day pre-conflict baseline) for four or more consecutive weeks

kill_conditions.condition: Qatar's Ras Laffan helium/LNG production resumes at scale
kill_conditions.metric: QatarEnergy production/export capacity disclosures
kill_conditions.threshold: QatarEnergy confirms LNG/helium export capacity restored to at least 90% of pre-strike levels

kill_conditions.condition: Helium spot and contract prices normalize
kill_conditions.metric: Spot and contract helium price indices
kill_conditions.threshold: Spot prices fall back within 20% of pre-March-2026 levels for two consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Industrial gas majors report helium turning from headwind to tailwind
kill_conditions.metric: Air Products and Linde quarterly segment commentary on helium
kill_conditions.threshold: Both companies report helium as a net margin positive (not a headwind) for two consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Alternative supply scales fast enough to replace lost Qatari volume
kill_conditions.metric: Independent helium supply-demand balance trackers (e.g. Smith, Fusion, industry gas-market research)
kill_conditions.threshold: Trackers report the global deficit closing to within 5% of the pre-crisis supply-demand balance

statement: PJM's FERC-filed Interim Resource Adequacy Service / BYONC curtailment framework is not itself the bottleneck -- it is a rationing mechanism that reveals a genuine, pre-existing structural bottleneck in firm, dispatchable generation capacity within the largest US grid, evidenced by a more-than-tenfold rise in PJM's capacity-auction clearing price (to a record $333.44/MW-day) and PJM's first-ever failure to clear its full reliability requirement (a ~6,623MW shortfall). Because gas-turbine lead times (three-plus years, backlogs into 2029-2031 at GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Power) gate the BYONC self-generation path, the policy allocates existing scarcity toward better-capitalized developers rather than creating new supply. Its durability is genuinely contested: the binding mechanism does not apply until June 1, 2027, applies only to new loads, FERC has not yet ruled, and PJM previously retreated from a similar mandatory bring-your-own-generation proposal to a voluntary one after 2025 stakeholder pushback.

kill_conditions.condition: FERC rejects or materially waters down PJM's IRAS/BYONC proposal
kill_conditions.metric: FERC order on Docket ER26-3380
kill_conditions.threshold: FERC denies the mandatory curtailment-priority framework, requires it be made voluntary, or orders substantial revisions removing the BYONC-linked curtailment priority

kill_conditions.condition: PJM's capacity-auction reliability shortfall closes
kill_conditions.metric: PJM Base Residual Auction cleared capacity vs. Reliability Requirement
kill_conditions.threshold: A subsequent PJM capacity auction fully clears its Reliability Requirement with no shortfall

kill_conditions.condition: Gas-turbine lead times shorten materially
kill_conditions.metric: Reported order-to-delivery lead time at GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Power
kill_conditions.threshold: Quoted lead times fall below 2 years at two or more of the three major OEMs

statement: A severe and geographically concentrated shortage of skilled construction trades -- especially electricians, whose work spans roughly half of all on-site labor on AI data-center projects -- has emerged as a structural constraint on US AI data-center construction that is distinct from, and in some respects more immediate than, the chip-packaging, memory, grid-equipment and interconnection-policy bottlenecks this pipeline has previously examined, evidenced by record contractor backlogs (EMCOR +44%, Comfort Systems USA +73%, Quanta Services +50% YoY in Q2 2026), a multi-hundred-thousand-worker shortfall estimate, and direct multi-hundred-million-dollar hyperscaler intervention (Microsoft, Meta) to train new workers rather than wait for the market to supply them.

kill_conditions.condition: Electrician wage growth and job-opening projections normalize toward historical trend
kill_conditions.metric: YoY electrician wage growth (Indeed data) and BLS projected annual openings/growth rate
kill_conditions.threshold: Wage growth falls back below roughly 3% YoY and BLS's projected openings/growth rate is not revised upward

kill_conditions.condition: Training pipeline programs demonstrably close the shortfall gap
kill_conditions.metric: Reported graduate/placement counts from Microsoft-NABTU, Meta's Workforce Academy and comparable programs versus the 500,000+ estimated electrician shortfall
kill_conditions.threshold: Verified graduate/placement counts reach a material share (tens of thousands) of the estimated shortfall within 2 years

kill_conditions.condition: AI hyperscaler capital-expenditure guidance decelerates materially, reducing new data-center construction starts and therefore labor demand
kill_conditions.metric: Aggregate hyperscaler capital-expenditure growth guidance (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon)
kill_conditions.threshold: Aggregate guided capex growth decelerates materially quarter over quarter

statement: Organized local, state and tribal opposition -- roughly 38 New Jersey municipal bans, 70-100+ local moratoria nationwide, New York's Executive Order 62 statewide permitting pause, a ~200 GW Texas interconnection freeze, Indianapolis's binding moratorium through 2027, and a ban by the Cherokee Nation -- is a distinct, fast-proliferating 'permission' bottleneck on US AI data-center buildout that cannot be resolved with capital alone. Because developers can generally relocate to another jurisdiction, it is structurally hard only at the level of a specific already-committed site (interconnection queue position, water rights, fiber proximity), not at the national portfolio level, where the ~$64 billion blocked/delayed to date remains a small share of total US data-center capex. Its durability is already being tested by a court ruling that struck down one moratorium (Imperial County) and by state legislatures where 13 of 14 tracked statewide moratorium bills have failed to pass.

kill_conditions.condition: Courts strike down a critical mass of local/state moratoria following the Imperial County precedent
kill_conditions.metric: Share of litigated moratoria overturned versus upheld
kill_conditions.threshold: A majority of litigated moratoria are struck down within the next 12 months

kill_conditions.condition: The rate of new local moratoria/bans plateaus or reverses
kill_conditions.metric: Net new local moratoria enacted per month, minus repeals
kill_conditions.threshold: Net new enactments fall to zero or go negative for two consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Congress or the federal government adopts binding preemption of state/local data-center zoning and moratoria
kill_conditions.metric: Passage of federal preemption legislation or a court ruling establishing federal preemption
kill_conditions.threshold: Enacted preemption law or controlling appellate ruling

statement: China's near-total control of yttrium and erbium processing -- yttrium exports to non-China markets down roughly 75% year-on-year in 2026 and European erbium prices up over 50% since June -- has created a materials-level bottleneck feeding two AI-buildout-critical supply chains this pipeline has previously examined only from other angles: gas-turbine power generation (yttria thermal barrier coatings) and data-center optical networking (erbium-doped fiber amplifiers). Demand is high, supply elasticity is low given China's near-total processing share, and near-term substitutability is hard for the highest-purity applications, meeting the strict structural-bottleneck test. But the constraint is unusually reversible: it traces to a negotiated trade-truce suspension expiring November 10, 2026 rather than physical scarcity, China has favored targeted company-specific measures (blacklisting MP Materials and USA Rare Earth) over blanket cutoffs, and non-China alternative separation capacity, while nascent, is already commissioning.

kill_conditions.condition: China extends or removes the export-control suspension on all five second-wave elements without new restrictions
kill_conditions.metric: MOFCOM/GACC announcement status on Nov 10, 2026 deadline
kill_conditions.threshold: Suspension extended or controls formally lifted with no new restrictions imposed

kill_conditions.condition: Non-China heavy-rare-earth separation capacity scales materially faster than current targets
kill_conditions.metric: Combined MP Materials/Lynas/USA Rare Earth reported nameplate and actual output for yttrium/erbium-bearing heavy REEs
kill_conditions.threshold: Combined non-China capacity reaches at least 15% of estimated global yttrium/erbium demand within 18 months

kill_conditions.condition: China escalates to broad, blanket rare-earth export restrictions covering yttrium and erbium with no licensing pathway
kill_conditions.metric: Scope and enforcement severity of any new MOFCOM/GACC announcement
kill_conditions.threshold: Blanket restriction imposed with minimal license approvals sustained for a full quarter

statement: AI training data, checkpoints and inference logs have driven hyperscaler demand for nearline HDD and enterprise NAND/SSD capacity to a level that has sold out hard-drive production through 2026-2028 and pushed NAND/SSD prices up 50-100%+ over the past year, meeting the strict Structural Bottleneck test at the NAND-fab layer while remaining more contestable at the HDD-assembly layer, where QLC SSD substitution already provides some elasticity; unlike geology- or permitting-bound bottlenecks, both binding layers face a defined, capital-backed capacity response (Seagate's HAMR ramp, the $31B Kioxia/SanDisk Japan investment) already underway.

kill_conditions.condition: Seagate reaches its 70% HAMR nearline penetration target on or ahead of schedule and reports shortening lead times for new orders
kill_conditions.metric: HAMR % of nearline exabyte run rate; new-order lead times
kill_conditions.threshold: 70%+ HAMR penetration reported with lead times returning to pre-2025 norms

kill_conditions.condition: TrendForce or equivalent trackers report NAND/DRAM contract prices flattening or declining quarter-over-quarter
kill_conditions.metric: NAND/DRAM QoQ contract price change
kill_conditions.threshold: Two consecutive quarters of flat or declining contract prices

kill_conditions.condition: Hyperscalers cancel or materially scale back long-term storage supply agreements
kill_conditions.metric: Reported LTA cancellations or capex pullback commentary
kill_conditions.threshold: Any major hyperscaler discloses reduced or canceled multi-year storage commitments

statement: Chinese AI firms are legally exploiting a gap in US export-control law -- renting access to export-controlled Nvidia Blackwell GPUs through data centers in Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia and Japan rather than importing the physical chips -- producing documented billion-dollar deals even after Nvidia's direct China sales fell to roughly zero market share. The House passed the Remote Access Security Act 369-22 in January 2026 and Commerce's BIS drafted a rule targeting the same loophole for as early as September 2026, but the bill remains stalled in the Senate and BIS may lack authority to act alone, making the enforcement mechanism itself -- not physical chip supply -- the binding structural bottleneck, racing against China's own domestic AI-chip ramp (Huawei Ascend).

kill_conditions.condition: The Senate passes S. 3519/H.R. 2683 and it is signed into law, giving BIS clear statutory authority over remote access
kill_conditions.metric: Bill passage status
kill_conditions.threshold: Senate floor vote plus presidential signature

kill_conditions.condition: Huawei/domestic Chinese AI chip makers reach or exceed a sustained ~90% share of China's AI chip market with confirmed frontier-training-capable output
kill_conditions.metric: China domestic AI chip market share
kill_conditions.threshold: Sustained 90%+ domestic share with evidence of frontier-scale training capability

kill_conditions.condition: BIS formally publishes the drafted remote-access rule as an enforceable regulation covering third-country GPU rental
kill_conditions.metric: Federal Register publication status
kill_conditions.threshold: Final or interim final rule published

statement: Broadcom's Q3 FY2026 results (reported September 2, 2026) beat the ~$16 billion AI semiconductor revenue guide the original CoWoS-bottleneck thesis assumed, with AI semiconductor revenue reaching $16.7 billion (+221% YoY) and management introducing unprecedented FY2027/FY2028 targets of $115 billion and $230 billion -- guidance that itself implies Broadcom is scaling design and shipment capacity roughly 4x from FY2026 to FY2028, evidence of high rather than low supply elasticity at the design layer. TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is separately reported narrowing from roughly 20% to 10% by end-2026, and OpenAI's first Broadcom-designed accelerator (Jalapeno) shipped in Q3 FY2026 without a packaging-related delay -- together downgrading the packaging layer from Structural Bottleneck to Growth Area. What remains genuinely unresolved is customer and design-partner concentration: Broadcom's backlog and multi-gigawatt commitments (Anthropic ~5GW, OpenAI 10GW by 2029, Meta 3GW) run through just six hyperscale customers and almost exclusively Broadcom's own design capability. This concentration is a material bear-case risk, but the available evidence -- Broadcom's own rapidly scaling guidance and Jalapeno's on-schedule shipment -- does not yet show the wait-times, rejected customers, or delayed tape-outs needed to classify Broadcom's design/integration capacity itself as a proven Structural Bottleneck; it remains a medium-confidence inference worth continued validation rather than an established finding.

kill_conditions.condition: TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap fails to narrow further, or industry trackers report it widening again
kill_conditions.metric: Industry-reported CoWoS supply-demand gap percentage
kill_conditions.threshold: Gap remains at or above roughly 15-20% past end-2026, reversing the reported narrowing trend

kill_conditions.condition: A qualified competitor (e.g., Marvell) or an in-house hyperscaler design team wins a large new multi-gigawatt custom-accelerator program away from Broadcom
kill_conditions.metric: Disclosed new custom-ASIC design wins by non-Broadcom vendors
kill_conditions.threshold: Any disclosed multi-gigawatt program awarded to a competitor

kill_conditions.condition: Broadcom's actual Q4 FY2026 or FY2027 results materially miss the newly raised guidance
kill_conditions.metric: Reported AI semiconductor revenue vs. guided figure
kill_conditions.threshold: Miss of guidance by a material margin for one or more quarters

kill_conditions.condition: OpenAI's Jalapeno or Anthropic's Ironwood-based deployments slip in Q4 2026/2027 with packaging or component constraints explicitly cited as the cause
kill_conditions.metric: Reported shipment timelines and cited causes for any delay
kill_conditions.threshold: Any disclosed delay explicitly attributed to packaging/component supply

statement: Texas (Governor Abbott's August 3, 2026 directive), Pennsylvania (Executive Order 2026-05, August 18) and Ohio (AEP Ohio's data-center tariff) have each moved to freeze or gate new data-center grid interconnections in response to 'ghost demand': a Reuters review found large-load electricity requests exceeding 700 gigawatts nationally and 474 gigawatts in Texas alone, over five times peak demand and roughly a tenfold rise since 2023, which regulators attribute largely to duplicative or unfunded speculative filings rather than real demand. This is a distinct bottleneck mechanism from the political-opposition moratoria and PJM curtailment-priority rules this pipeline covered in August 2026 -- an administrative queue-integrity problem, not a physical shortage or a community veto. The evidence -- a concrete ~December 2026 audit target, AEP Ohio's tariff already cutting its pipeline by more than half, and Vistra's dedicated Comanche Peak-Amazon supply deal demonstrating real substitutability -- indicates this functions as a temporary, substantially self-correcting Growth Area friction rather than a proven Structural Bottleneck.

kill_conditions.condition: ERCOT completes its audit substantially on schedule (around December 2026) and clears a large majority of queued projects, resuming Batch Zero processing at or near its pre-freeze pace
kill_conditions.metric: Share of audited Texas interconnection requests cleared and Batch Zero resumption date
kill_conditions.threshold: Audit completed within 1-2 months of the ~December 2026 target with resumed processing

kill_conditions.condition: Verified, financed demand within the audited queue turns out to be a large majority of the original 474GW headline figure
kill_conditions.metric: Disclosed verified vs. total requested capacity
kill_conditions.threshold: Verified demand exceeds roughly half of headline requested capacity

kill_conditions.condition: Multiple additional major data-center states adopt comparable interconnection-queue freezes or audits
kill_conditions.metric: Number of states adopting comparable queue-verification measures
kill_conditions.threshold: 2 or more additional major data-center states within 2-3 quarters

statement: CXMT's global DRAM share reportedly reached ~10% in Q2 2026 (versus ~7% cited by this pipeline's August 22, 2026 report for the same quarter) and it began small-batch, unqualified HBM3E shipments to two domestic Chinese customers in September 2026. This follow-up finds the gains concentrated in commodity DRAM -- a node already classified Neutral because its tightness stems from Samsung's and SK Hynix's own reallocation toward HBM4 -- while CXMT's HBM3E remains unqualified, one generation behind, and on the same ~2027 mass-production timeline already on record, not ahead of it. The HBM4 Structural Bottleneck classification from the August 22 report is reaffirmed and, if anything, strengthened: Samsung's entire 2026 HBM4 capacity is reported sold out and spot HBM prices are running roughly five times contract levels. A new, independent thread -- US revocation of Samsung's and SK Hynix's China Validated End-User status, an annual export-license review, and a reported targeted-tariff threat -- adds a separate supply-elasticity risk to those firms' legacy China-based fabs that could offset rather than reinforce any easing CXMT's rise might otherwise imply.

kill_conditions.condition: CXMT achieves confirmed qualified, volume HBM3E or HBM4-class production with at least one design win outside mainland China
kill_conditions.metric: Confirmed non-Chinese customer qualification or design win for CXMT HBM output
kill_conditions.threshold: At least one disclosed qualification or design win outside China

kill_conditions.condition: BIS tightens or fails to renew the annual export-license review for Samsung's or SK Hynix's China fabs, or the reported tariff threat materializes
kill_conditions.metric: BIS license-review outcome; confirmed tariff action
kill_conditions.threshold: Any confirmed license denial, material new restriction, or enacted tariff

statement: 3M's 2022 exit from PFAS-based fluorochemical manufacturing, discontinuing the Novec and Fluorinert fluids that underpinned nearly all commercial two-phase immersion cooling, removed the dominant fluid supplier for AI data centers' most thermally efficient cooling technology just as AI accelerator thermal design power escalates toward the multi-kilowatt-per-chip range. Multiple 2026 regulatory developments -- an EPA TSCA PFAS reporting deadline pushed to October 2026, the EU's ECHA advancing a broad REACH PFAS restriction toward a Commission decision, and multibillion-dollar PFAS litigation exposure -- compound the supply-side uncertainty. However, this does not yet meet the strict Structural Bottleneck test: single-phase, PFAS-free direct-to-chip cooling already commands the majority of the liquid-cooling market and needs no dielectric fluid; Microsoft and Meta are reported to have paused two-phase R&D over the fluid uncertainty; and a replacement fluid, Chemours' HFO-based Opteon 2P50, already has a 2026 manufacturing agreement with Navin Fluorine International and is in a full-scale customer trial. This is a genuine but narrow, largely self-resolving constraint the industry is routing around via technology substitution -- one that could become more binding only if rack densities force broad two-phase adoption faster than the replacement-fluid supply chain can scale.

kill_conditions.condition: A major hyperscaler or AI data-center operator discloses a project delay, cancellation, or capacity shortfall explicitly attributed to two-phase dielectric cooling fluid unavailability
kill_conditions.metric: Disclosed capacity/delay impact attributed to cooling-fluid supply
kill_conditions.threshold: At least one confirmed disclosure

kill_conditions.condition: Chemours' Opteon 2P50 manufacturing ramp with Navin Fluorine International slips materially beyond its disclosed 2026 timeline, or the NTT DATA/Hibiya Engineering trial is discontinued
kill_conditions.metric: Opteon 2P50 commercialization status
kill_conditions.threshold: Confirmed delay or discontinued trial

kill_conditions.condition: Two-phase immersion cooling's share of new AI data-center liquid-cooling deployments grows materially toward or beyond 20% as rack densities rise past 500kW, despite the fluid-supply uncertainty
kill_conditions.metric: Two-phase immersion cooling share of new liquid-cooling deployments
kill_conditions.threshold: Share reaches or exceeds 20% of new deployments

statement: ASML's sole-source monopoly on EUV lithography systems -- 100% EUV share and ~94% overall lithography share, built over roughly 30 years with no competitor ever commercializing a rival system -- meets every criterion of the strictest Structural Bottleneck test (Extreme demand growth, Low supply elasticity, Hard substitutability), making it arguably the most extreme monopoly bottleneck in the AI accelerator supply chain. However, unlike this pipeline's other confirmed Structural Bottlenecks (HBM memory), the evidence indicates this one is currently latent rather than proximate: ASML has grown EUV shipments over 45% year-over-year in 2026 and committed to further 30% capacity increases in both 2027 and 2028, broadly matching disclosed foundry demand, while trade press explicitly names advanced packaging and HBM memory -- not lithography tool availability -- as 2026's acute, binding AI chip supply constraints. September 2026's High-NA EUV commitments from TSMC (2030), Samsung (2028 DRAM) and Intel (already in production) signal rising per-chip lithography-step intensity that could tighten the capacity-to-demand ratio over time, and escalating US pressure on the Netherlands to fully ban ASML's China sales adds a distinct geopolitical variable, but as of this report ASML has out-invested visible demand rather than fallen behind it.

kill_conditions.condition: A foundry customer (TSMC, Samsung, or Intel Foundry) explicitly attributes an AI chip production shortfall to EUV/High-NA EUV tool unavailability rather than packaging, HBM, power, or labor constraints
kill_conditions.metric: Primary cited cause of AI chip capacity shortfall in company disclosures
kill_conditions.threshold: At least one explicit primary-source disclosure naming lithography tool availability as the binding constraint

kill_conditions.condition: ASML's disclosed backlog or 2027/2028 EUV capacity expansion plans are materially cut back or delayed
kill_conditions.metric: ASML capacity guidance and backlog disclosures
kill_conditions.threshold: A confirmed downward revision to the 30%/30% 2027-2028 capacity plan or a backlog decline

kill_conditions.condition: Canon's nanoimprint lithography or China's domestic EUV program achieves a qualified production win at a leading-edge node
kill_conditions.metric: Qualified production adoption of a non-ASML lithography technology at the leading edge
kill_conditions.threshold: At least one confirmed qualification/production announcement

kill_conditions.condition: The Dutch government enacts a full ban on ASML sales and servicing to China, including DUV tools
kill_conditions.metric: Scope of Dutch/US export-control decision
kill_conditions.threshold: Full ban enacted covering DUV sales and servicing

statement: A cluster of 2026 disclosures -- rising global 8-inch foundry utilization (toward 90%), successive rounds of mature-node wafer price increases, and Q2 2026 earnings from Texas Instruments, onsemi, GlobalFoundries and Vanguard International Semiconductor all citing AI-driven demand for power-management ICs, power discretes, and analog/networking chips -- indicate that mature-node (8-inch and legacy 12-inch) foundry capacity has quietly become a genuine Structural Bottleneck on the AI buildout by the strict test (Extreme demand growth, Low supply elasticity, Hard substitutability for power ICs specifically), even though it receives far less market attention than the advanced-node, packaging, and memory layers this pipeline has previously examined. Vanguard's new Singapore fab selling out its entire first production phase before mass production begins is the clearest evidence of tightness. The bottleneck's durability is genuinely contested: nearly 70% of new mature-node capacity investment is concentrated among Chinese foundries rather than incumbents serving non-China AI supply chains, and mature-node shortages have historically proven cyclical (as in 2021-2022) rather than permanent.

kill_conditions.condition: Global 8-inch foundry utilization falls materially from the reported 88-90% range
kill_conditions.metric: Top-10 foundry 8-inch utilization rate (TrendForce)
kill_conditions.threshold: Utilization falls below 80% for two consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Texas Instruments, onsemi, or GlobalFoundries report AI/data-center-linked revenue growth decelerating sharply
kill_conditions.metric: Quarter-over-quarter data-center/comms-infrastructure revenue growth at each company
kill_conditions.threshold: Any of the three reports growth deceleration to below 20% YoY for two consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Chinese mature-node foundry capacity scales fast enough to supply non-China AI-exposed customers at volume
kill_conditions.metric: Disclosed qualification of Chinese mature-node foundries by non-China analog/power-IC suppliers
kill_conditions.threshold: At least one confirmed qualification/design win for global (non-China) AI-server supply chains

statement: South Korea's 97.5% import dependency on Israeli-origin bromine -- the feedstock for the semiconductor-grade hydrogen bromide (HBr) etch gas used to carve every DRAM, NAND and HBM chip, concentrated in a single Dead Sea complex operated by ICL Group -- meets the strict Structural Bottleneck test on the geographic-concentration framing (high and rising electronics-driven demand, low near-term supply elasticity given the single dominant origin, hard substitutability for HBr in memory plasma etch). But 2026 already ran the real-world stress test: a Middle East-tension-driven price spike that peaked above $6,000/tonne in April 2026 has, by both ICL's and Albemarle's own Q2 2026 earnings calls, substantially normalized, and no source confirms any actual DRAM, NAND or HBM output reduction at Samsung, SK Hynix or Micron -- whose Q2 2026 revenue rose a record 257% year-over-year with no disclosed input-availability impact. This is a genuine, extreme concentration risk that has so far proven more resilient than the initial 2026 alarm implied, distinguishing it from this pipeline's confirmed helium and rare-earth bottlenecks where suppliers themselves describe persistent, unresolved tightness.

kill_conditions.condition: Bromine/HBr prices remain durably normalized well below the April 2026 peak with no further spike
kill_conditions.metric: China/regional spot bromine price
kill_conditions.threshold: Prices stay below $4,000/tonne for four or more consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Non-Israeli raw bromine sources (Jordan Bromine Company, Albemarle Arkansas, Chinese Shandong producers) scale and are qualified for Korean/Japanese semiconductor-grade HBr supply chains
kill_conditions.metric: Disclosed qualification of non-Israeli-origin bromine feedstock by Korean/Japanese HBr converters
kill_conditions.threshold: At least one confirmed qualification or supply agreement

kill_conditions.condition: A confirmed DRAM, NAND or HBM output disruption is publicly attributed to bromine/HBr shortage
kill_conditions.metric: Company disclosures (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron)
kill_conditions.threshold: At least one confirmed disclosure of an output or shipment impact

kill_conditions.condition: Middle East tensions re-escalate specifically threatening Israeli Dead Sea bromine extraction or export infrastructure
kill_conditions.metric: Reported disruption to ICL's Dead Sea (Sodom) operations or Mediterranean export routes
kill_conditions.threshold: Confirmed production or export disruption

statement: Record 2026 earnings and raised guidance from Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA and Tokyo Electron -- all citing AI-driven demand pushing calendar-2026 wafer-fab-equipment spending to the low-$150 billion range and 2027 toward $190 billion -- have combined with TrendForce's August 19, 2026 report of deposition/etch/test tool lead times stretching to 24 months to create a rare opening for Chinese domestic toolmakers, whose global WFE share has risen from 1.2% (2021) to 6.5% (2025). For leading-edge, non-Chinese fabs (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, Micron, SK Hynix), this node plausibly meets the strict Structural Bottleneck test: demand is Extreme, supply elasticity is Low given multi-year capacity-expansion timelines at the four dominant Western/Japanese suppliers, and substitutability is Hard because Chinese tools remain unqualified for leading-edge processes and are barred by export control from non-Chinese fabs in any case. But the evidence is mixed: Tokyo Electron's own disclosed lead times actually shortened in 2026, all four major OEMs are expanding capacity aggressively, and no source found ties a specific TSMC, Samsung, Intel, Micron or SK Hynix capacity delay directly to equipment delivery rather than construction or demand planning -- meaning this may be a documented capacity squeeze without yet being a proven binding constraint on AI chip output.

kill_conditions.condition: Major WFE OEM lead times normalize across the board
kill_conditions.metric: Disclosed order-to-delivery lead times at Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA and Tokyo Electron
kill_conditions.threshold: Below 12 months sustained for 2+ consecutive quarters

kill_conditions.condition: Backlog-to-revenue ratio at major WFE OEMs declines materially
kill_conditions.metric: Reported backlog / deferred revenue
kill_conditions.threshold: 2+ consecutive quarters of decline

kill_conditions.condition: Major fabs proceed on stated 2026-2027 capacity timelines with no equipment-attributed delay disclosed
kill_conditions.metric: TSMC/Samsung/Intel/Micron/SK Hynix capacity-timeline disclosures
kill_conditions.threshold: Stated targets met with no equipment-delivery cause cited for any slippage

kill_conditions.condition: Chinese domestic tools achieve confirmed qualification or an order from a non-Chinese fab
kill_conditions.metric: Disclosed qualification or purchase order outside China
kill_conditions.threshold: 1+ confirmed instance
